whatsNew.i18nDesc: Complete English and French translations across the entire UI
whatsNew.helpDesc: In-app documentation with guides for every module
whatsNew.onboardingDesc: Guided setup for new users with step-by-step onboarding
whatsNew.a11yDesc: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and high contrast support
whatsNew.brandingDesc: Fresh SandForge identity with updated logo and icons
whatsNew.syncFidelityDesc: Direction, filters, field types and transform rules are all checked before a run writes anything
whatsNew.themesDesc: Text and badge colours now clear AA contrast on the VS Code themes we test, light and dark
whatsNew.accents: Spanish, Portuguese and German keep their accents
whatsNew.accentsDesc: Hundreds of strings had lost them; a gate now watches every language
whatsNew.speedDesc: Fewer round trips to Salesforce on each refresh and each graph discovery
whatsNew.honestyDesc: Tabs, modes and options that led nowhere are gone, so what you see is what runs
whatsNew.stylesheet: The panel looks like itself again
whatsNew.stylesheetDesc: 1.23.0 shipped without its stylesheet, so every screen rendered as bare HTML. A check now reads the files the extension links to and asks the disk for each one.
whatsNew.syncWrites: A sync writes the fields it read
whatsNew.syncWritesDesc: A configuration with no field mapping wrote empty records, and Quick Sync matched on a key the target org had never issued — so no run could succeed.
whatsNew.failureReason: A failed run tells you why
whatsNew.failureReasonDesc: The reason is kept on the history entry, next to the objects the run had already written before it stopped.
whatsNew.forgeProgress: Forge no longer shows the last run\u2019s progress
whatsNew.forgeProgressDesc: Node statuses are cleared when a run starts, a skipped object counts as finished, and the time remaining is measured on the work that settled.
whatsNew.deadKeys: Sixteen labels showed their own translation key
whatsNew.deadKeysDesc: The Autopilot legend, the sync history status and trigger columns and a queued node read as text again, in all six languages.
whatsNew.templateRoot: A Forge template clones the record you name
whatsNew.templateRootDesc: The built-in templates say they clone one record and everything around it, but nothing asked which record — so the run copied whole tables instead. The Template tab now asks.
whatsNew.perObjectMapping: Map every object, not just the first
whatsNew.perObjectMappingDesc: Whatever you mapped was attached to every object of the run, so only one object could really be mapped. Each now keeps its own, and an object you leave unmapped is copied field for field.
whatsNew.describeOnce: An object is described once, not twice
whatsNew.describeOnceDesc: A Quick Sync described its objects to build the mapping and the run described them all over again. Each describe carries its own timeout, and running out of one ends the run.
whatsNew.orgsCrashDesc: An org saved by an older build could crash the page as it loaded. Stored orgs are now given the shape the app expects as they are read.
whatsNew.forgeCounts: Forge fills in the counts as it reads them
whatsNew.forgeCountsDesc: A run started from a template showed no record or field counts on its graph, for the whole run. They now arrive as each object is read.
whatsNew.uncopyable: Users and metadata are no longer offered for copying
whatsNew.uncopyableDesc: Salesforce reports User, UserRole and RecordType as creatable, so runs tried to copy them — a user costs a licence and a unique username. One rule now covers every module.
whatsNew.liveStatsDesc: The records and API-call counters sat at zero for the whole run and jumped to their final value at the end. Each object now reports what it wrote as it finishes.
whatsNew.cloneDuplicates: A clone can write into a sandbox that already looks like the source
whatsNew.cloneDuplicatesDesc: Every clone of an Account was refused by a duplicate rule before writing anything, and the whole graph below it was skipped. A clone now tells Salesforce it means to duplicate; a unique index still refuses, which is right.
whatsNew.ownerMap: A cloned record keeps the owner you mapped it to
whatsNew.ownerMapDesc: The flag that remaps an owner onto a target user did nothing in the one case it exists for — records authored by someone who is not on the target sandbox. The record arrived with no owner at all. It now arrives with the one you asked for.
whatsNew.deferredScope: A clone reaches the records it depends on
whatsNew.deferredScopeDesc: An object reached only through one of its own children — a price book behind an opportunity's line items — was read as empty and its lookups left dangling. It is now asked again once the rest of the run has found what points at it.
whatsNew.sidePanelPlace: The side panel knows where you are
whatsNew.sidePanelPlaceDesc: The module you are on now looks selected, the org list closes on Escape or a click elsewhere, a favourite can be removed from the Favourites list, and the panel no longer says no org is connected while it is still asking.
whatsNew.scopedRead: A clone reads only what it can write
whatsNew.scopedReadDesc: A price book entry reached through its product could belong to a price book the run never creates; read, it travelled all the way to the insert and was refused there. A scoped read now has to stay inside the parents the run has actually read.
whatsNew.fullProductClone: An opportunity with products clones completely
whatsNew.fullProductCloneDesc: Account, price book, products, prices and line items, with the amounts that follow. The path had never worked: the standard price book was copied instead of matched, its prices were missed, and the line items were written before the entries they point at.
whatsNew.keyboardEverywhere: Every control in the panel answers the keyboard
whatsNew.keyboardEverywhereDesc: Conversations in the AI panel are real buttons now, the graph controls stopped listening for the mouse, and the accessibility rules that were warnings while the count came down from 86 to zero are errors.
whatsNew.syncFinishes: A sync can finish a job
whatsNew.syncFinishesDesc: Run against a real pair of orgs for the first time, Sync could not write one record: it sent every field it read, it did not say its rows were meant to resemble the ones already there, and one lookup the target did not have cost the whole record. All three are fixed.

help.title: Help & Resources
help.gettingStartedContent:
1. Connect your Salesforce org using the Organizations page.
2. Open the Monitor to check your org health.
3. Use Seed to generate test data in your sandbox.
4. Set up Sync to keep environments in sync.
5. Explore Compare, DataOps, and Automation for advanced workflows.
help.monitorContent:
The Monitor dashboard shows real-time org health:
- Health Score gauge with contributing factors
- API limits with usage trends and predictions
- Active and recent Apex jobs
- Alert notifications for critical thresholds

Tip: Enable auto-refresh for continuous monitoring.
help.seedContent:
The Seed wizard generates realistic test data:
1. Select your target org
2. Choose objects to seed
3. Configure field rules (AI, Faker, static, sequence...)
4. Set record counts — a lookup field is filled from the records the same run inserted earlier
5. Review and execute

Tip: Use AI generation for the most realistic data.
help.syncContent:
Sync data between two Salesforce orgs:
- Full sync only: every run replays the whole object set (incremental, delta and CDC are not implemented)
- Auto field mapping with confidence scores
- Transform rules apply to every field of every record of the run, except Id and the external ID the run matches on, which are left as they are so a prefix or a truncate cannot send the write to a record that does not exist. The settings each one takes: case and trim take none; truncate takes a length; prefix, suffix, replace, regex, default value, date and number formats and formulas take their text; value mapping takes a table of replacements the page cannot type yet, so a rule of that kind leaves values as they are
- Conflict resolution on bidirectional runs: source wins, target wins, newest wins or a field-level merge
- No undo: a run cannot be reversed, so take a DataOps backup of the target org first (it covers Account and Contact)
help.compareContent:
Compare metadata between two orgs:
- Diff viewer grouped by category and risk level
- Permissions: which profiles and permission sets exist on each side
- Snapshots: the objects of both orgs, captured live when you open the tab
- Drift: five Organization settings side by side (name, language, locale, time zone, fiscal year start)
- Deploy: coming soon, nothing is deployed from a diff yet
help.dataopsContent:
Data operations on the selected org:
- Backup: a full snapshot of Account and Contact, kept in extension storage
- Restore: puts a backup back, whole, into the org it was taken from
- Anonymize: masks fields in place with a built-in template such as GDPR, CCPA or HIPAA; it cannot be undone, so back up first
- Compliance, Cleanup and Quality: coming soon, nothing runs behind these tabs yet
help.automationContent:
Visual pipeline builder:
- 15 step types in 4 categories. Only Delay and Condition do anything yet: the other 13 report success without touching an org
- Pipelines start by hand, from the Run Pipeline button; nothing else starts one yet
- Condition steps with 11 operators
- Execution history: status, total duration, step count and errors for each run
- Pipeline templates from the Marketplace
help.forgeContent:
Forge clones a real record, and the records around it, from one org into another:
1. Paste a record ID or Salesforce URL, then pick the source and target orgs
2. Discover Graph walks the relationships from that record
3. Set the depth, the records per object and PII anonymization
4. Review the plan, then run it: IDs are remapped as the records are written; a record type with no active record type of the same API name on the target keeps its source Id, and the SandForge log names it

Tip: a record-scoped clone copies what that record needs, not whole tables.
help.frozenContent:
Frozen Dataset extracts a dataset from a source sandbox once and replays it after every refresh:
- Extract: root records chosen by coverage matrix, within a volume budget
- Pseudonymization is deterministic, keyed by a salt you keep out of the repository
- A four-point check must pass before the dataset is written
- Load: sandbox targets only, with an optional Pilot on one root folder before the full load, and a verification pass after the load
help.grappeContent:
Grappe splits a large operation into partitions and reports progress as each one completes:
- Turn it on with the sandforge.grappe.enabled setting
- A Seed run past the record threshold reports each partition, a Sync past it reports one partition per object, and an Autopilot run reports only its start and its end
- Partitions run one after another: Grappe does not make a run faster
help.aiContent:
AI Assistant, with your own Anthropic key:
- Chat, and NL2SOQL, custom personas and AI field rules in Seed
- Pipeline drafts in Automation
- A built-in table of Salesforce error codes answers the codes it knows first, on your machine, AI on or off, and sends nothing
- Nothing is sent for a fixed list of SandForge's own messages, such as a declined production confirmation, a duplicate run, or a CRUD, FLS or Production Guard refusal, nor for any failure while no SandForge view is open
- While AI is on, any other failed Seed, Sync, DataOps or Automation run sends its error message, with its Salesforce Ids replaced by <id>, and the suggestion comes back as a VS Code notification
- Turn that sending off with sandforge.ai.errorResolution: the rest of the assistant keeps working
- Compare's schema advice and Monitor's anomaly scan are rule-based: they run with AI off and no key
- Configure your API key in Settings > AI
help.shortcutsContent:
G + letter — Jump to a module (e.g. G then F for Forge, G then Y for Sync, G then L for Help)
Ctrl+K — Command palette
Escape — Close modals and dialogs
Tab — Navigate between elements
Enter/Space — Activate buttons and links
help.faqContent:
Q: Why is my Health Score low?
A: Check API limit usage, failed jobs, and storage consumption. The score weighs multiple factors.

Q: How to fix timeout errors?
A: SandForge has no timeout setting for Salesforce calls. Lower the batch size (sandforge.seed.defaultBatchSize and sandforge.sync.defaultBatchSize in VS Code Settings) and split a large run into smaller ones. Grappe does not make a run faster: it reports progress per partition.

Q: Can I undo a sync operation?
A: No. A sync run cannot be reversed. Before a risky run, take a DataOps backup of the target org: it covers Account and Contact, and restores only into that org.

Q: How do I connect a production org safely?
A: Production orgs are auto-detected and marked as Critical safety tier. All destructive operations require confirmation.
help.troubleshootingContent:
Connection Issues:
- Verify your Salesforce credentials are valid
- Check your IP whitelist settings
- Ensure your session has not expired

Performance Issues:
- Check API usage in Monitor before a large run
- Split a large run into several smaller runs
- Reduce batch size for complex operations

Data Issues:
- Verify field-level security (FLS) permissions
- Check for required fields that may be missing
- Review governor limits in Monitor dashboard

history.reused: Form refilled from the run of {{date}}.

duplicateValue.explanation: A record with the same unique value already exists in the target org, often one cloned by an earlier run.
duplicateValue.action: Delete the records the earlier run created, or run the clone from the command line with --upsert, which updates by external ID where the object has one.

invalidCrossReferenceKey.explanation: A lookup points to a record that does not exist in the target org, often a user such as the owner.
invalidCrossReferenceKey.action: Create or map the referenced record in the target org, or leave the lookup empty and set it after the clone.

requiredFieldMissing.explanation: A required field has no value: {{detail}}.
requiredFieldMissing.action: Turn on "Auto-fetch parents", or raise the depth so the required parent is part of the clone.

invalidPicklist.explanation: A picklist value from the source does not exist in the target org's picklist.
invalidPicklist.action: Add the value to the picklist in the target org's Setup, or change the value on the source record.

invalidFieldForInsert.explanation: A field cannot be set on create: it is calculated, hidden by field-level security, or missing from the target org.
invalidFieldForInsert.action: Check field-level security for your user in the target org, and compare the field between the two orgs.

fieldIntegrity.explanation: Salesforce rejected the record on an integrity rule: {{detail}}.
fieldIntegrity.action: Read the detail: Salesforce usually names the field or the rule involved.

cannotInsertEntity.explanation: Salesforce does not accept new records of this object (a history, audit or system object).
cannotInsertEntity.action: Leave this object out of the clone.

insufficientAccess.explanation: Your user in the target org lacks the access this write needs.
insufficientAccess.action: Ask an administrator for the missing permission, or connect the target org with a user that has it.

storageLimit.explanation: The target org has no data storage left.
storageLimit.action: Delete records you no longer need from the target org, then run again.

invalidType.explanation: This object does not exist in the target org, or your user cannot see it.
invalidType.action: Compare the two orgs' schemas, or leave this object out of the clone.

notFound.explanation: Salesforce could not find the requested record or resource.
notFound.action: Check the record ID and that it belongs to the source org.

stringTooLong.explanation: A value is longer than the field allows: {{detail}}.
stringTooLong.action: Shorten the source value, or give the field the same length in both orgs.

cycleFkUnresolved.explanation: Field '{{fieldName}}' points to a parent that was not cloned (source ID {{sourceRefId}}), so the record was created without that link.
cycleFkUnresolved.action: Raise the depth so the parent is part of the clone, or set the field by hand afterwards.

standardPriceMissing.explanation: Salesforce will not price a product in a custom price book until that product has a price in the standard one, and the standard entry is not in the target org.
standardPriceMissing.action: Add a standard price for these products in the target org, then run the clone again.

recordTypeUnavailable.explanation: The record type exists in the target org and was matched correctly, but it is not available to the user the clone runs as.
recordTypeUnavailable.action: Assign the record type to that user's profile in the target org, or exclude the RecordTypeId field for this object.

outOfScope.explanation: None of the parent records this object hangs from are in the clone, and it is not the root object, so none of its records were cloned.
outOfScope.action: Raise the depth if you need records of this object in the clone.

unknown.action: Look up this error code in the Salesforce documentation.

forge.soqlObjectNameInvalid: "{{object}}" is not an SObject API name, so the WHERE clause cannot be sent under it. It must start with a letter and hold at most 80 letters, digits or underscores.
forge.hintSoqlObjectNameInvalid: Fix the object name after FROM to discover the graph
forge.truncatedRead: Read only in part: {{objects}}. The source holds more rows than were cloned — split the run with filters that each stay under the bound to clone the rest.
